notice_lobby.title: Notice on the lobby board
notice_lobby.text:
OVERNIGHT SUPPORT SERVICE · FERRIER COURT

FINAL NIGHT

From 06:00 on Saturday 26 September, every resident of Ferrier Court is covered by their Designated Personal Contact under the DPC Scheme. The Overnight Support Service will close.

Your new Community Responder, ARI, begins duties at 06:00.

Thank you for thirty-five years.
Community Services

(Written underneath in biro:) WHO IS ARI??
(And in the bottom corner, in pencil, in different writing:) ask jad

tobi_drawing.title: Tobi's drawing
tobi_drawing.text:
Crayon on sugar paper.

A tall person in an enormous brown coat, arms out, next to a building with a lot of windows. Above it: ARI.

Where the face should be there's nothing: a clean oval, carefully coloured round.

Along the bottom: A PERSON WHO HELPS IN OUR COMMUNITY. BY TOBI AMADI 3B.

On the back, in the same crayon: I LEFT THE FACE FOR LATER.

leaflet_arrivals.title: Leaflet: Arrivals (sent by Sal)
leaflet_arrivals.text:
ARRIVALS: A GUIDE FOR NEW PERSONS
Community Services leaflet A/7

Some people arrive without the usual.

If you have come into being through a telephone line, a public address system, a radio frequency or another means of address, you may be an arrival.

You are a person. You are entitled to register. Registration gives you a name in law, a record, and access to services.

You may be offered work. You do not have to accept work in order to register.

Where to go: Arrivals & Registration, Community Services (now part of Transition).
Receiving rooms: most have closed. Please ask.

(Clip art: a smiling telephone with arms.)

photo_arrivals.title: Photograph: Arrivals, winter 1958
photo_arrivals.text:
FERRIER ST. BATHS · ARRIVALS · WINTER 1958

Six people in towelling robes sitting on the pool steps, each holding a card with a number on it. Their feet are bare on the wet tiles. One of them is laughing so hard the camera has blurred her.

Inez: "The one laughing is Mrs. Doyle. Third floor till ninety-four."

photo_attendants.title: Photograph: Municipal Attendants, 1965
photo_attendants.text:
MUNICIPAL ATTENDANTS · FERRIER ST. BATHS · 1965

Eleven men in a row along the pool edge, in the same jacket and the same cap, photographed so they come out the same.

They aren't the same. One has a ring on his little finger. One's cap is on crooked. The fourth from the left is smiling. The fifth is holding his hands together in front of him like someone still waiting to be told something.

poster_received.title: Poster: The Received Person
poster_received.text:
THE RECEIVED PERSON
What to expect in your first week
(Ministry of Health, 1956)

You will be hungry. This is normal. Eat little and often.
You will be cold.
You may not recognise your reflection. This is normal. Do not stare at mirrors for long periods; your face will settle.
You may hear the line for some weeks. This will fade.
Rest.
Registration is your right. Ask the attendant.

(A diagram of a body, drawn stiffly, by someone who had only ever had one described to them.)

jad_letter.title: Jad's letter
jad_letter.text:
To every household at Ferrier Court, and to Community Services.

I filled in the DPC-1 forms for nine households in August, at a table in the lobby. Where people had nobody who could promise to come, I wrote ARI, the name from the council's sample form, and gave a number that rang in the building.

There was no Ari. The forms were my idea and my handwriting. The people who signed them did so because the council asked them to name somebody and they were frightened of losing help.

The Overnight Support Service was closed on the grounds that every resident had a contact. That wasn't true, and it isn't their fault. I'd like the closure looked at again.

Jad Mansour, Flat 4B

(Printed at Aldine Copy & Print, 04:12. 42 copies. Paid.)
